headline: Anthropic offers $100 credit after Fable 5's chaotic rollout and new pricing tiers
summary: Anthropic is giving a one-time $100 credit to Pro and Team Standard subscribers after Fable 5 moved to a pay-as-you-go model, with usage costing $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens.
details: Fable 5, part of Anthropic's new Mythos tier, launched with additional safety measures around biology, cybersecurity, and LLM R&D. It was initially released on June 9, 2026, alongside Mythos 5.

Just three days after its release, Anthropic suspended access to Fable 5 to comply with U.S. Department of Commerce export controls. Access was later restored on July 1, following the lifting of these controls.

The rollout remained unsettled due to higher-than-anticipated demand, making compute capacity difficult to predict. Anthropic expanded availability in stages, temporarily pulling back and then restoring access multiple times.
This led to weeks of uncertainty where users couldn't predict their access from one day to the next. The company extended free access multiple times as more capacity came online.

Permanent access rules were finally established on July 20, 2026. Max and Team Premium plans now include Fable 5 at no extra cost, capped at approximately 50% of the plan's normal weekly usage limits.

For Pro and Team Standard plans, Fable 5 transitioned to pay-as-you-go usage credits, no longer bundled into the flat monthly fee. Enterprise Premium seats get Max-equivalent treatment, while Standard seats require admin-enabled usage credits.

To ease this transition, Pro and Team Standard users received a one-time $100 credit, automatically applied. This credit was claimable between July 20 and August 2, 2026, and expires on September 19, 2026.

Once the credit is depleted, Fable 5 bills at API rates: $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens. This makes it the steepest-priced Claude model currently in general availability, roughly double the cost of Opus 4.8.

The $100 credit can be used quickly; a single heavy session generating around 2 million output tokens could consume the entire credit. While generous for exploration, it is not a long-term substitute for regular workflow if Fable 5 becomes essential.

headline_marked: [[Apple services face widespread outage]] for some users, now fixed after second incident this week
headline: Apple services face widespread outage for some users, now fixed after second incident this week
summary: For the second time this week, Apple's App Store, iTunes Store, and other services experienced a widespread outage affecting users and developers. The issue has since been resolved.
details: Apple faced a widespread outage affecting its App Store, iTunes Store, and other services. This marks the second such incident within a single week, impacting both end-users and developers.

The issues were initially reported by users experiencing difficulties accessing various Apple platforms. Apple's system status page eventually confirmed the disruptions, though specific causes were not immediately detailed.

While the outage has now been resolved, the repeated occurrences raise questions about the stability of Apple's infrastructure. Users were unable to download apps, make purchases, or utilize developer tools during the downtime.
